question: In the United States, which kills the most people each year: car crashes, drug overdoses, alcohol or smoking?
answer: Smoking, by far: about 480,000 American deaths a year, the CDC estimates, nearly one death in five. Alcohol follows at about 178,000. Overdoses make headlines because they kill the young, suddenly; tobacco kills slowly, decades after the first cigarette, mostly late in life, so each death is recorded as an ordinary illness.
move: A killer that works slowly looks like bad luck; count it anyway.
reference: CDC, Health Effects of Cigarette Smoking (more than 480,000 deaths a year); Esser et al. (2024) Deaths from excessive alcohol use, United States, 2016-2021, MMWR 73(8); NCHS Data Brief, Drug overdose deaths in the United States, 2002-2022; NHTSA, Traffic Safety Facts 2022
ask: Which risk in my own life do I treat as normal because it kills slowly?

items.label: Drug overdoses
items.note: About 107,000 in 2022, the peak year; most involved fentanyl.

items.label: Smoking
items.note: About 480,000: more than the other three put together.

items.label: Alcohol
items.note: About 178,000: more than overdoses, and far less talked about.
